correctness.rationale: The 16 dinucleotides form four self-reverse-complement fixed orbits AT,TA,CG,GC plus six nonfixed pairs. Ten windows are necessary, and the exhibited length-ten cycle meets the bound. Equality entails one edge per orbit, so exactly 2^6=64 oriented edge choices. Degree balance leaves 24 edge sets, all with positive directed tree cofactor. The directed BEST and matrix-tree factors group as eight each of 36,12,20 cyclic tours, totaling 544. Complement flips all six chosen nonfixed edges, so has no fixed rotation class; the order-16 symmetry action has Burnside fixed values 544,24,24 only, yielding 37, with orbit sizes 31x16+6x8. Independent brute-force enumerated all 4^10=1048576 rooted strings and obtained 5440 accepted rooted strings, 544 rotations, 272 RC orbits, 37 total symmetry classes. Circle/linear boundary remains explicit.

value.rationale: The first nontrivial even window problem for Watson–Crick reverse-complement covering has a literature-motivated enumeration question and a natural complete finite design space. The complete 544-cycle catalogue and two physically relevant symmetry quotients distinguish designs and support subsequent probe-constraint optimization. The exact fact is not an arbitrary slice; the minimum length and all competing optima are both resolved.
